title: Token flow & headroom matrix — Q3 2026 modeling
summary: This modeling sheet converts regional QPS forecasts to tokens/sec and GPU-equivalent capacity, then applies explicit headroom targets to produce reserved GPU commitments for Hosted API. It focuses on mixed generation workloads (avg token lengths 50–90) and shows sensitivity to batching and kernel/quantization variance.
assumptions: 1) Baseline GPU performance (H100-equivalent) = 20,000 tokens/sec for our mix (median model family, 12-20 token generation latency path). 2) Average tokens per request by region are estimated from routing logs (30-day window) and include both prompt+generation. 3) Effective batching & KV cache achieves an incremental 15% throughput vs no-batch baseline; the 20k figure is post-batching conservative. 4) Surge multipliers represent short peak windows (10–30 min). 5) Headroom target is applied to baseline steady-state capacity to avoid cold oversubscription during regional surges or failovers.
methodology_notes:
- Baseline GPU equivalent 20k tokens/sec is conservative; A100-like fleets should be treated as ~12–15k tokens/sec for this workload, H100 ~18–25k depending on kernel. We intentionally use 20k to avoid underprovisioning.
- Baseline_gpus_needed = ceil(baseline_tokens_per_sec / 20000).
- Surge_gpus_needed = ceil(surge_tokens_per_sec / 20000).
- Gpus_with_headroom = ceil(baseline_gpus_needed * (1 + target_headroom_pct/100)).
- Reserved_gpu_pool rounds up to the next whole slice (we keep 1 GPU granularity per region for Dedicated pools).
- KV cache hit assumptions: 25% effective token reduction for repeated prefixes; reduce tokens/sec accordingly for conversational-heavy customers (not applied in table; see sensitivity).
sensitivity_summary: 1) If effective per-GPU throughput drops to 18k tokens/sec (kernel/quantization delta), total baseline GPUs increase from 29 -> 29*20000/18000 ≈ 32 (add ~3 GPUs). 2) If avg tokens/req increases by 25% during a product-driven campaign, baseline tokens/sec grows to ~648k and GPUs baseline -> 33. 3) Batching loss (from 15% to 0%) reduces per-GPU effective capacity and increases reserved by ~12%.
recommendations:
- Reserve region-level pools as shown in reserved_gpu_pool column (sized for baseline + 30% headroom). This keeps peak failover capacity local and minimizes cross-region cold startup.
- Maintain a 10–15% global emergency buffer (separate floating pool) for multi-region failover events.
- Introduce 'fast-fallback' rule: during sudden 3x spikes, route non-SLA traffic to lower-cost quantized variants automatically. Track quality/regression alerts with Redwood Optimize.
- Run a kernel-profile sweep on the most-used model in each region to validate the 20k tokens/sec assumption; target tests on H100 and the highest-availability GPU in the pool.

risks_and_open_questions:
- Model mix shift risk: onboarding a heavier-generation model family (x2 tokens average) will break these headroom targets; flag onboarding for a re-run.
- Inter-region routing delays and cold-starts could cause short-term token bursts beyond modeled multipliers; consider a 1-hour throttle for new releases.
- Do we prefer to keep headroom as percent of GPUs or percent of tokens/sec? Current ops favors percent of GPUs for simpler rounding.
- Validation needed: compare table to last 90-day peak window traces (Jira INF-4321).
notes: Quick notes to reviewers: this sheet is intentionally conservative on per-GPU throughput and liberal on headroom. It is targeted at the Hosted API business where SLA stability during unpredictable peaks matters more than minimizing short-term cost. If leadership prefers tighter economics, we can re-run with 20% headroom and a 22k tokens/sec per-GPU assumption.
